changelog: Fix: the Linux client installer never worked on Debian 12/13 (issue #19). St0r generated its own bash script that called `apt-key` (removed in Debian 12) and `lsb_release` (not installed by default), pointed at an apt repository that has no packages for those releases, and then wrote the client config to /etc/default/urbackupclient in a format the UrBackup client does not read — using the web port 55414 instead of the internet port 55415, and never enabling internet mode. Even where it installed, the client could not connect.

The Linux download now serves the same pre-configured, self-extracting installer that the UrBackup web UI hands out — the one confirmed working on Debian 13 — with this client's name, server address, internet port and auth key already baked in. It ships prebuilt binaries and needs no apt repository, so it works across distributions. Run it with `sudo sh urbackup-client-<name>.sh`.
Windows and Linux installers now share one code path, so both get the same validation and error handling.

Requesting an installer for a client id that does not exist in UrBackup now returns a clear error instead of a generic installer carrying the global auth key and no client name — which would install but never register as the intended client.
Installer download failures are shown in the page instead of being silently saved as a broken file, and the Linux download tells you the exact command to run.
